Q: Coding Academy quiz, Lesson 27 (Counting Patterns). Predict the exact output of this code, then answer the questions:

gems = ["ruby", "opal", "opal", "jade", "ruby", "opal", "jade"]
counts = {}
for g in gems:
    counts[g] = counts.get(g, 0) + 1
print(counts["opal"])
print(len(counts))
print(counts.get("pearl", 0))
print(max(counts, key=counts.get))

1. The printed lines, in order.
2. In one sentence: what does counts.get(g, 0) do that counts[g] cannot?
3. What does plain max(counts) with no key= return here, and why is it the wrong answer for most frequent?

A: 1. The printed lines, in order:
   ```
   3
   4
   0
   opal
   ```

2. In one sentence: `counts.get(g, 0)` provides a default value of 0 if the key `g` does not exist in the dictionary, preventing a `KeyError` that would occur with `counts[g]`.

3. `max(counts)` with no `key=` returns the alphabetically largest key in the dictionary, which is "ruby" in this case. This is the wrong answer for the most frequent gem because `max(counts, key=counts.get)` correctly identifies the key with the highest value (i.e., the most frequent gem), which is "opal".

An 8 m circle collapses inward: every enemy inside is dragged to the centre, takes 200% ability damage and is stunned for 1 s.  **How it should look — the ART BRIEF.**  > Total darkness at the aim point. A single white-hot pinprick ignites dead centre, so bright it has a violet halo. In the next half-second the space around it *bends*: fine streaks of starlight and silver dust that were drifting lazily in the circle are caught and pulled, curving into long spiral trails that all wind inward toward the point like water round a drain — the trails get tighter and faster and their colour shifts from white to violet as they fall in. They are read out of the engine, not typed here.  ## 3.1 · Stats per level A hero's stat line is **base + per-role growth x (level-1)** — additive, not multiplicative. Anything without a role growth row falls back to **x(1 + 0.05 x (level-1))**.  | role | HP / lv | ATK / lv | AP / lv | armor / lv | MR / lv | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | **Tank** | +34 | +0.9 | +0.3 | +12 | +8 | | **Bruiser** | +22 | +1.6 | +0.4 | +8 | +6 | | **Assassin** | +15 | +2.2 | +0.3 | +5 | +4 | | **Marksman** | +13 | +2 | +0.4 | +4 | +4 | | **Support** | +13 | +0.5 | +1.6 | +4 | +7 | | **Mage** | +11 | +0.6 | +2 | +3 | +8 |  **Default armour / MR when a hero declares none:**  | role | armor | MR | |---|---|---| | Tank | 60 | 40 | | Bruiser | 40 | 30 | | Assassin | 25 | 20 | | Marksman | 22 | 22 | | Mage | 15 | 40 | | Support | 22 | 38 |  **Mitigation gets harder with level:** `defToDR(r) = r/(r+K)` where `K = 1200 + 17.4 x (level-1)`. The same armour buys less damage reduction as you climb, so defence must keep growing to hold value.  ## 3.2 · Skill levels  **A skill can never pass its hero's CURRENT level** (Phil, 12 Sep 2026). The cap is the level cap, and the hero's own level is the running ceiling — enforced on the client in `skillUpgrade()` and on the server in `/api/skill/upgrade` against `ledHeroLevel`.  **Every skill level adds +1.35% of the skill's base effect**, to level 100. `skillMul(lv) = 1 + (lv-1) x 0.0135` — so **Lv 100 = x2.337** of the Lv 1 numbers. This multiplies the SCALING values (damage, damage/sec, heals, shields). **Cooldowns, durations, stun and slow times do NOT scale with skill level** — they are fixed per ability.  ## 3.3 · Stars and refine | | | | | | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1★ x1.00 | 2★ x1.15 | 3★ x1.35 | 4★ x1.60 | 5★ x1.90 |  **Refine anchors** (5★ · Bronze · Silver · Gold, 5 refine steps per tier): x1.90 · x2.25 · x2.65 · x2.90  ---  # GLOSSARY — LESSONS LEARNED  Why the rules read the way they do.  ## THE 49-HERO PARSE — 11 HEROES REPORTED “BUILT BUT UNREACHABLE” (12 Sep 2026) A brace-walker stopped at the first closing brace of `HERO_TYPES`, saw **49** heroes instead of 60, and produced a false report to Phil that **eleven heroes were built but unreachable in the shipped game** — escalated at the time as “the largest thing in the archive”. They were fine: the v332 batch (1-2 Sep), all `locked:true` with `start:2`/`start:3` — **unlock gating, not absence.** Two rules came out of one mistake: never parse the engine (RULE 2), and locked is not missing (RULE 6). The comment blocks also contain apostrophes that break naive string tracking, so even a careful walker is unsafe.  ## WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AT ALL Phil, 12 Sep 2026: *“There needs to be a hero index clearly identifying heroes to you, then the hero index needs to be in the master protocol index.”* · *“The hero index should even have the glyph and equipment path, base stats, how much base stats gained per level. Skills, how much percent of damage, heals, shield, stun time, etc etc goes up per level of the skill.”* · *“Everything about that hero.”* It is generated rather than written because a hand-kept copy of the engine drifts from the engine, and a drifted copy is worse than none — it gets cited.  ## THE ULTIMATE NAME CONFLICT `tools/hero_extras/ultimates.md` is Phil’s earlier pass and is **stale on names**: 39 of 59 match the engine, 20 do not, and on 17 of those 19 checked the engine matches his own design packs. So the engine wins on names (RULE 7) — but the file’s **“what it does”** and **“how it should look”** text is still his brief and is reproduced per hero. A conflict is printed inline rather than silently resolved.  ## ALL HEROES CRIT — ONLY MELEES HAVE A CRIT CLIP This is a ROSTER rule, not a combat rule (`07 - COMBAT PROTOCOL` owns the combat side). A ranged hero showing `—` under crit has been read as a missing animation more than once; it is correct.  ## THE ANNOTATOR HAS NO PASSIVE BY DESIGN Not a gap, and not to be “fixed”. Recorded here because chapter 1’s gap tables would otherwise imply one.  ## THE NAMES The engine keys and the in-game names diverge for eight heroes, and Phil has asked many times that the in-game name is used in every message and every document. The key belongs in a code fence, next to the name — never instead of it.  ---
